'''Edward Gill III''' (born August 16, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Gill played [[college basketball]] at the [[College of Eastern Utah]], [[Salt Lake Community College]], and [[Weber State University]]. With the [[Weber State Wildcats men's basketball|Weber State Wildcats]], Gill was [[most valuable player|MVP]] of the 1999 [[Big Sky Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Sky Conference tournament]].

Not selected in the [[2000 NBA draft]], Gill began his professional career with the [[Las Vegas Silver Bandits]] of the [[International Basketball League (1999–2001)|IBL]] and debuted with the [[New Jersey Nets]] of the [[NBA]] late in the {{nbay|2000}} season. Gill has had a [[Journeyman (sports)#American English|journeyman]] career in basketball and has played in various teams in the NBA, [[NBA Development League]], minor leagues, and overseas. In the NBA, Gill has played for the New Jersey Nets, [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Seattle SuperSonics]], and [[Milwaukee Bucks]] all usually in [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]] roles. However, Gill has been a starter and high scorer for much of his non-NBA career. Professionally, Gill has been an All-Star selection in the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] (2004) and [[NBA Development League]] ([[2008 NBA All-Star Game#D-League All-Star Game|2008]]) and won championships with the D-League (2009 with the [[Colorado 14ers]]) and [[Belgian Basketball Cup|Belgian Cup]] (2010 with [[BC Oostende]]).

Won a regional Emmy award for his work as an analyst on Pacers Live Pregame.

==Early life and college==
Gill was born in [[Aurora, Colorado]], and graduated from [[Overland High School]] in 1996. After high school, Gill enrolled at the [[College of Eastern Utah]], a [[junior college]] in [[Price, Utah]], and played on the basketball team, averaging 6.1 points and 2.4 assists. In 1997, Gill transferred to [[Salt Lake Community College]] and again played basketball. At Salt Lake CC, Gill had 16.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 6.4 assists per game.<ref name="D-League bio"/>

Gill transferred to [[Weber State University]] in 1998 and played for two seasons on the [[Weber State Wildcats men's basketball]] team. In his junior year (1998–1999), Gill averaged 14.0 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 4.5 assists.<ref name="D-League bio"/> For the 1999 [[Big Sky Conference men's basketball tournament]], Gill was [[most valuable player|MVP]] after scoring 15 points and making 9 assists and 6 rebounds in 40 minutes of play. He also only committed two of his team's five turnovers in the 82–75 victory over [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]]I despite playing 40 minutes. This tournament championship qualified Weber State for an automatic [[1999 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]] bid.<ref name="field of 64">{{cite news|last=Eborn|first=Jared|title=Wildcats to join field of 64; Weber State beats Northern Arizona to gain automatic NCAA bid|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/684385/Wildcats-to-join-field-of-64.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022071232/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/684385/Wildcats-to-join-field-of-64.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 22, 2013|access-date=January 9, 2013|newspaper=Deseret News|date=March 7, 1999}}</ref> In the Round of 64 game, 14th-seeded Weber State upset third-seeded [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] 76–74.<ref>{{cite web|last=Eborn|first=Jared|title=Surprise! Weber St. knocks off North Carolina|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/685209/Surprise-Weber-St-knocks-off-North-Carolina.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065901/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/685209/Surprise-Weber-St-knocks-off-North-Carolina.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 22, 2013|work=Deseret News|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=March 12, 1999}}</ref> Gill scored 16 points despite only making 4 of 12 field goals; he also made 5 of 5 [[free throw]]s and had 2 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 5 defensive [[Rebound (sports)|rebounds]].<ref>{{cite web|title=(14) Weber State 76, (3) North Carolina 74|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/1999-03-11-north-carolina.html|work=sports-reference.com/cbb|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> In Weber State's next round loss to sixth-seeded [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], Gill scored 19 points in 5-for-14 shooting and 7-for-8 free throw shooting and also made 3 defensive rebounds and 5 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=(14) Weber State 74, (6) Florida 82|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/1999-03-13-florida.html|work=sports-reference.com/cbb|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Weber State finished the season 25–8.<ref>{{cite web|title=1998–99 Weber State Wildcats Roster and Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/weber-state/1999.html|work=sports-reference.com/cbb|access-date=January 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121222031813/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/weber-state/1999.html|archive-date=December 22, 2012}}</ref>

As a senior (1999–2000), Gill averaged 16.3 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 6.9 assists. In both seasons, Gill earned First-Team All-[[Big Sky Conference]] honors.<ref name="D-League bio">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill|url=http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/eddie_gill.pdf|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Las Vegas Silver Bandits, Kansas City Knights, New Jersey Nets, and Italy (2000–2001)===
Not selected in the [[2000 NBA draft]], Gill began his professional career with the [[Las Vegas Silver Bandits]] of the [[International Basketball League (1999–2001)|IBL]]. In 31 games with Las Vegas, Gill averaged 14.1 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 6.9 assists. Gill then played in 10 games with the [[Kansas City Knights]] of the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|ABA]] and averaged 6 points and 9 assists. On March 29, 2001, Gill signed a 10-day contract with the [[NBA]]'s [[New Jersey Nets]] and would sign another 10-day contract afterwards.<ref name="basketball reference">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gilled01.html|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Playing in a game against the [[Boston Celtics]] on April 15, 2001, Gill scored the eight millionth point in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|title=Boston 95, New Jersey 88|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/recaps/2001/04/15/bos_njn/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011123224543/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/recaps/2001/04/15/bos_njn/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 23, 2001|work=CNN.com|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> With New Jersey, Gill averaged 4.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.3 turnovers in 8 games. He made 39% of field goals.<ref name="basketball reference"/> Gill joined the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] team [[Fortitudo Pallacanestro Bologna|Paf Bologna]] in April 2001.<ref name="eurobasket">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill basketball profile |url=http://dmlpj02vd15xf.cloudfront.net/fileadmin/user_upload/_temp_/11.07.15_Player_Profile_Eddie_Gills.pdf |publisher=eurobasket.com |date=July 15, 2011 |access-date=January 9, 2013 }}{{dead link|date=December 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Return to Kansas City and Memphis Grizzlies (2001–2002)===
Returning to the Kansas City Knights in fall 2001, Gill played in 18 games and averaged 12.1 points, 4.9
rebounds, and 6.7 assists.<ref name="D-League bio"/> Gill signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for a 10-day contract on February 23, 2002, and later signed for the rest of the {{nbay|2001}} season.<ref name="basketball reference"/> Gill played 23 games with Memphis and started 5. He averaged 5.0 points, 1.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.5 turnovers.<ref name="basketball reference"/> In a game that used only eight players, Gill scored 20 points in his debut with Memphis on February 25, a 90–77 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LA Clippers 90, Memphis 77|url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2002/02/25/LA-Clippers-90-Memphis-77/UPI-86101014696721/|publisher=UPI|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=February 25, 2002}}</ref> Gill made 7 of 12 field goals (including 1 of 2 three-pointers) and made all 5 free throw attempts. He also had 5 rebounds, 7 assists, and a steal.<ref name="2001-02 games">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill 2001–02 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gilled01/gamelog/2002/|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Gill would score in double figures in only three other games: 11 on March 3 against [[Seattle SuperSonics|Seattle]], 11 on March 4 against [[Atlanta Hawks|Atlanta]], and 10 on March 7 against [[Indiana Pacers|Indiana]].<ref name="2001-02 games"/>

===D-League and Italy (2002–2003)===
Gill signed with [[NBA Development League]] team [[Tulsa 66ers|Asheville Altitude]] on November 23, 2002, and was waived on February 24, 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=2002–03 Transactions|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/transactions_0203.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131124054120/http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/transactions_0203.html|archive-date=November 24, 2013}}</ref> Gill played 35 games with Asheville and averaged 12.5 points and 5.2 assists.<ref name="D-League bio"/> Gill later signed with [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Reggio Emilia]] of the Italian league [[Legadue Basket]] and averaged 14.1 points
and 2.9 rebounds in 13 games.<ref name="D-League bio"/>

===Greek League, CBA, and return to NBA (2003–2004)===
In the beginning of the {{nbay|2003}} season, Gill played with [[Greek Basket League]] team [[Ionikos NF BC|Ionikos Athens]]. In six games, Gill averaged 15.8 points and 3.7 assists. He later played in 25 games for the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] and averaged 18.1 points and 8.0 assists.<ref name="D-League bio"/> In the CBA All-Star Classic on January 20, Gill helped the National team rally from a 20-point deficit to a 2-point win with 15 points, 6 assists, 10 rebounds, and 3 steals.<ref name="Pacers 2004">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill page: 2004-05 Player HQ|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/gill_page_0405.html|publisher=Indiana Pacers|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref>   Gill returned to the NBA on February 5, 2004, by signing as a free agent with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. In 22 games, Gill averaged 2.3 points, 0.8 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.<ref name="basketball reference"/>

===Indiana Pacers (2004–2006)===
On June 24, 2004, Portland traded Eddie Gill to the [[New Jersey Nets]], but the Nets waived Gill on July 6. Gill signed as a free agent with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on July 28.<ref name="basketball reference"/> In the infamous game on November 19, 2004, that concluded with the [[Pacers–Pistons brawl]], Gill joined two of his Pacers teammates and others in an effort to break up a fight between players and fans.<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|title=Timeline of Pacers-Pistons brawl|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1927833|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=November 20, 2004}}</ref> The following day, Gill started the game and was one of only six players used due to the suspensions from the brawl the night before.<ref name="2004-05 games"/><ref>{{cite web|author=Herman, Steve (Associated Press)|title=Magic deflate shorthanded Pacers|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/games/2004-11-20-pacers-magic_x.htm|work=USA Today|date=November 21, 2004|access-date=January 10, 2013}}</ref> In Indiana's 86–83 loss to [[Orlando Magic|Orlando]] on November 20, Gill made 3 of 10 field goals (including 1 of 1 three-point attempt), converted 1 of 2 free throws, and had 8 points, 1 rebound, 3 assists, 3 steals, and a turnover.<ref name="2004-05 games"/> Gill played in 73 games in {{nbay|2004}} and had 3 starts in the {{nbay|2004}} season for the Pacers and averaged 3.7 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.<ref name="basketball reference"/> Gill scored a season-high 21 points on December 1 against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref name="2004-05 games">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill 2004–05 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gilled01/gamelog/2005/|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Gill made his postseason debut on April 23, 2005, in the Pacers' first first-round playoff game against the [[Boston Celtics]]. Gill made one field goal out of four attempts and made two free throws; in 17 minutes of play he scored 4 points and made 2 rebounds, 2 assists, a steal, and 2 turnovers.<ref name="2004-05 games"/> In the {{nbay|2005}} season with Indiana, Gill played only 41 games an averaged 1.1 points, 0.4 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.<ref name="basketball reference"/>

===Dynamo Moscow (2006–2007)===
For the {{nbay|2006}} season, Gill again played overseas, for [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]] of [[Russian Basketball Super League]]. He averaged 7.3 points and 2.5 assists in 33 Russian League games and 6.2 points and 1.4 assists in 20 [[Euroleague]] games.<ref name="D-League bio"/>

===Return to the Nets and D-League, Seattle SuperSonics (2007–2008)===
On October 1, 2007, Gill signed with the [[New Jersey Nets]] but was waived on October 25.<ref name="basketball reference"/><ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Transactions (October 25, 2007)|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/transactions/_/date/20071025|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> The [[Colorado 14ers]] drafted Gill as the top pick in the [[2007 NBA Development League Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dleague_draft_071102.html|title=Colorado 14ers Select Eddie Gill With Top Pick In 2007 D-League Draft|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105185411/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dleague_draft_071102.html|archive-date=November 5, 2012}}</ref> Due to a thigh injury to [[Darrell Armstrong]], the Nets re-signed Gill on November 16.<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|title=Nets sign Gill to fill in for injured guard Armstrong|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3114007 |work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2007|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> With New Jersey, Gill averaged 2.9 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.6 assists before the Nets waived him on December 12.<ref name="basketball reference"/> In his short stint, Gill had two games in double figures: 12 points on 4-for-5 shooting on November 19 against [[Utah Jazz|Utah]] and 10 points on December 4 against [[Cleveland Cavaliers|Cleveland]].<ref name="2007-08 games">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill 2007–08 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gilled01/gamelog/2008/|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Gill also started the December 5 game against [[New York Knicks|New York]].<ref name="2007-08 games"/> Gill returned to the Colorado 14ers on December 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top Overall Pick Eddie Gill Returns To Colorado 14ers|url=http://cache.nba.com/dleague/colorado/gill_071217.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=December 17, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022040544/http://cache.nba.com/dleague/colorado/gill_071217.html|archive-date=2013-10-22|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 37 games with Colorado, Gill averaged 18.0 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 8.5 assists.<ref name="D-League stats">{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill Career Stats and Totals |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/career.jsp?player=eddie_gill |publisher=NBA D-League |access-date=January 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026223418/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/career.jsp?player=eddie_gill |archive-date=October 26, 2013 }}</ref> In the 2008 [[NBA D-League All-Star Game]] on February 16, Gill played on the Red Team and scored 3 points off one three-pointer but missed 6 other field goals. He also had 3 rebounds, 7 assists, and 2 turnovers. The Blue Team won 117–99 over Red.<ref>{{cite web|title=Red 99, Blue 117|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20080216/DLBDLR/boxscore.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109203010/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20080216/DLBDLR/boxscore.html|archive-date=November 9, 2012}}</ref>

On March 24, 2008, the Seattle SuperSonics signed Gill to a ten-day contract, due to a depleted lineup.<ref name=sonicssigning>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|title=Wilcox, Watson out vs. Blazers; Sonics sign guard Gill to 10-day deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3310297|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 24, 2008|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> He played only 5 minutes against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in his first game on March 24.<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280324025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160908221516/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280324025|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 8, 2016|title=Durant, Sonics dump Blazers, end 11-game slump|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2008}}</ref> On April 3, his contract expired and was not renewed.<ref name="basketball reference"/>

===Return to Colorado 14ers, call-up to Milwaukee Bucks (2009)===
He signed with the New Jersey Nets in the 2008 offseason but was waived, among with 3 other players, before the season started (October 24). He had averaged 4.5 points and 1 assist in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3661466|title=Van Horn, Gill, Hamilton, Hodge waived by Nets in roster moves|work=ESPN.com|date=October 24, 2008|access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Gill returned to the Colorado 14ers on December 8.<ref>{{cite web|title=Transactions|url=http://cache.nba.com/dleague/colorado/transactions.html|publisher=Colorado 14ers|access-date=January 9, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022041011/http://cache.nba.com/dleague/colorado/transactions.html|archive-date=2013-10-22|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The [[Milwaukee Bucks]], facing a depleted roster due to injuries, signed Gill to a 10-day contract on February 9, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sorgi|first=Jay|title=Bucks Sign Eddie Gill|url=http://www.todaystmj4.com/sports/45356142.html|work=TodaysTMJ4.com|publisher=WTMJ|access-date=January 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126025038/http://www.todaystmj4.com/sports/45356142.html|archive-date=2013-01-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He signed a second 10-day contract on February 20. In 6 games for the Bucks he averaged 2.8 points and 1.8 assists in 7.2 minutes per game.<ref name="basketball reference"/> This call-up to Milwaukee would end up being Gill's final days in the NBA, as his final NBA game was played on February 25, 2009, in a 96–116 loss to the Dallas Mavericks. In his final game, Gill played for 5 and half minutes and recorded 2 assists and 1 rebound.

In 40 games with Colorado, Gill averaged 14.8 points, 3.9 rebounds, 8.4 assists, and 1.6 steals.<ref name="D-League stats"/> D-League coaches voted Gill as Player of the Year at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colorado's Eddie Gill Earns NBA D-League Impact Player Award|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/impact_090407.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=April 7, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026223412/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/impact_090407.html|archive-date=October 26, 2013}}</ref> In Game 1 of the D-League finals on April 21, Gill made the tying free throw to force overtime, and Colorado beat the [[Utah Flash]] 136–131 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colorado 14ers defeat Utah Flash in game one of 2009 NBA D-League Finals|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/COLORADO_14ERS_DEFEAT_UTAH_FLA-310648-1172.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=April 22, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026223413/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/COLORADO_14ERS_DEFEAT_UTAH_FLA-310648-1172.html|archive-date=October 26, 2013}}</ref> Colorado won the D-League title in Game Two on April 23.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bodenrader|first=Mark|title=14ers Live in the Moment, Take 2009 NBA D-League Crown|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/14ers_champions_090424.html|publisher=NBA D-League|access-date=January 9, 2013|date=April 22, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026223415/http://www.nba.com/dleague/14ers_champions_090424.html|archive-date=October 26, 2013}}</ref>

===BC Oostende (2009–2010)===
In November 2009, Gill signed with the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Basketball League Belgium]] team [[BC Oostende]] and in 26 games averaged 7 points, 3. rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 2.2 steals with 28.0% field goal shooting.<ref name="eurobasket"/> On February 19, 2010, during a late 12–4 run by Oostende, Gill made five free throws in the last two minutes to seal a 75–68 win over the [[Antwerp Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Belgian League, Game 21: February 19–20, 2010 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216001716/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/euroleaguenews/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2009-2010/belgium/i/67239/3834/belgian-league-game-21-february-19-20-2010 |url-status=live |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |publisher=Euroleague |access-date=January 10, 2013 }}</ref>  Oostende won the Belgian Cup championship for the season.<ref name="eurobasket"/>

===EWE Baskets Oldenburg (2010–2011)===
On September 24, 2010, he signed with the [[New Jersey Nets]] of the [[NBA]] but was waived on October 6, 2010.<ref name="basketball reference"/> On December 6, 2010, Gill signed with [[Germany|German]] team [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]] for the remainder of the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/on-court/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/79775/4674/ewe-baskets-lands-eddie-gill |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122161209/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/on-court/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/79775/4674/ewe-baskets-lands-eddie-gill |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 22, 2013 |title=EWE Baskets lands Eddie Gill |publisher=Euroleague |date=December 6, 2010 }}</ref> Gill played in 27 league games and averaged 7.1 points, 2.2 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 1.4 steals with 40.9% field goals made. In 2 [[Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]] games, Gill averaged 5 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists, and 1.5 steals.<ref name="eurobasket"/>

===Townsville Crocodiles (2011–2012)===
On July 15, 2011, Gill signed with the [[Townsville Crocodiles]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australasia)|NBL]] for the [[2011–12 NBL season|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2011/july/crocs-snap-up-eddie-gill/ |title=Crocs snap up Eddie Gill |work=NBL.com.au |date=July 15, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222021051/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2011/july/crocs-snap-up-eddie-gill |archive-date=2011-12-22 }}</ref> In the 28 games of the regular season he averaged 12.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.4 steals in 29 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill|url=http://www.sportingpulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=194020288&client=0-189-88242-193068-11143963|work=SportingPulse.com|access-date=January 10, 2013}}</ref> Gill scored 21 in an October blowout 95–67 win over the [[Cairns Taipans]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Thompson|first=Michael|title=Steady Eddie|url=http://www.townsvillebulletin.com.au/article/2011/10/20/276251_sport.html|access-date=January 10, 2013|newspaper=Townsville Bulletin|date=October 20, 2011}}</ref>  On November 11, Gill led Townsville with 30 points and seven assists in Townsville's 95–88 overtime upset of the [[Melbourne Tigers]]; with 2 seconds left in regulation, Gill made the tying free throw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Crocs need overtime to kill off Tigers|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2011-11-11/crocs-kill-tigers-in-overtime/3662132|publisher=ABC News (Australia)|access-date=January 10, 2013|date=November 11, 2011}}</ref> With 73% field goals made, Gill scored 26 in a 100–93 win over the [[Sydney Kings]] on December 23.<ref>{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Antony|title=Eddie gets mojo back|url=http://www.townsvillebulletin.com.au/article/2011/12/24/293121_sport.html|access-date=January 10, 2013|newspaper=Townsville Bulletin|date=December 24, 2011}}</ref> Against doctor's orders, Gill played on March 4, 2012, with 15 stitches in his right hand. He had 4 points, 3 assists, and 7 turnovers but drew a last-second [[offensive foul|charging foul]] to seal Townsville's three-point victory over the [[Melbourne Tigers]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Antony|title=Gill's lesson in guts|url=http://www.townsvillebulletin.com.au/article/2012/03/06/311291_sport.html|access-date=January 10, 2013|newspaper=Townsville Bulletin|date=March 6, 2012}}</ref>

Gill won the NBL Player of the Week twice, in rounds 6 and 12,<ref>{{cite web|last=Howard |first=Marc |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2011/december/gill-wins-again/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907081346/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2011/december/gill-wins-again/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 7, 2012 |title=Gill wins again |publisher=NBL |date=December 27, 2011 }}</ref> and was also named to the 2011–12 All-NBL Third Team.<ref>{{cite web|author=Howard, Marc |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2012/march/lisch-wins-mvp/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120917141310/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2012/march/lisch-wins-mvp/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 17, 2012 |title=Lisch wins MVP |publisher=NBL |date=March 26, 2012 }}</ref>

The Crocodiles made it to the 2011–12 NBL playoffs, finishing in fourth position overall for the regular season with a win–loss record of 15–13 (54.57%). On Friday 30 March 2012, the Crocodiles scored an upset 99–82 win over the [[New Zealand Breakers]] in the first game of the 2011–12 NBL postseason competition. Gill scored 21 points, 4 steals, and 3 rebounds in the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2012/march/semi-final-report-crocs-shock-boardless-breakers/ |title=Semi-final Report: Crocs shock shaky Breakers |publisher=NBL |date=March 30, 2012 |access-date=January 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401235613/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/2012/march/semi-final-report-crocs-shock-boardless-breakers |archive-date=April 1, 2012 }}</ref>

Gill signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on October 1 but was waived before the regular season on October 27.<ref name="basketball reference"/> In three preseason games, Gill had limited playing time and made 0 of 4 field goals in one game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eddie Gill Game By Game Stats|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/eddie_gill/game_by_game_stats.html|publisher=NBA|access-date=January 10, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130516153959/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/eddie_gill/game_by_game_stats.html|archive-date=May 16, 2013}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Eddie Gill is married to Marisa and has two children: Eddie IV (born 2000) and Kiara (born 2002).<ref>{{cite web|title=Ex-Pacers guard Gill shares skills with kids|url=http://currentinwestfield.com/2014/ex-pacers-guard-gill-shares-skills-with-kids/|website=Current in Westfield|access-date=April 4, 2015|date=December 16, 2014|archive-date=April 3, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403054924/http://currentinwestfield.com/2014/ex-pacers-guard-gill-shares-skills-with-kids/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gill and his family have lived in [[Zionsville, Indiana]], since 2005. Since 2016, he has served as a studio analyst for Pacers games on FOX Sports Indiana.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Agness|first1=Scott|title=Gill joining FOX Sports Indiana as analyst|url=http://vigilantsports.com/fox-sports-indiana-televising-78-pacers-games-eddie-gill-to-join-network-as-an-analyst/|website=Vigilant Sports |access-date=October 5, 2016|date=October 5, 2016}}</ref>
